The only prerequisite is to complete 60 credits. That's all.
Usually, Cse311 is your baseline. But other courses help boost your knowledge. For example,
If you're interested in AI and ML: either of 445/465/468 or two
If you're interested in Hardware/Embedded: Cse331
Interest in Software: Cse327
Interest in Operating Systems: Cse323 and Cse332
Interest in Cybersecurity: Cse438 and Cse488
The courses are merely meant to give you the myriad possibilities in the CSE field. Think of it as getting better gear for your boss fight.
But that shouldn't stop you from doing any project you want. Take me as a reference, I haven't taken any Machine Learning course, yet I learned everything from scratch and built a pretty good ML project in less than 3 months. So, it's very feasible.
